editorial:
Imagine being so down in the dumps that you spend your days in pajamas watching kids' TV. That is where you meet Barry, a struggling actor who is going through a rough breakup and has zero luck in his career. Everything changes when he crosses paths with a bubbly children's show host at an awards show. Instead of being honest about his failing acting career, he panics and tells her he is a psychiatrist. It is a classic awkward setup that feels like a cozy romantic comedy, mixing a bit of sadness with plenty of laughs as Barry tries to keep up a total lie to win her heart.

You will love how the tension builds as Barry pretends to know things about the human mind that he actually does not. The acting is great and makes you really root for him even though he is lying through his teeth. The pacing is steady, though it feels more like a light TV movie than a big cinema production. If you want something relaxing to watch, you should try renting it on Apple TV or streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best picture quality. It is a sweet pick for a rainy afternoon.
endingExplained: Everything comes crashing down when the lie becomes too big to handle. Barry eventually has to admit that he is not a psychiatrist at all but just a struggling actor. Instead of being angry, the presenter appreciates his honesty and the effort he put into impressing her. They realize they actually have a real connection beyond the fake job. The movie ends on a happy note with the two of them starting a real relationship based on the truth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quirky romantic comedies about fake identities.
